chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abū Khālid al-Qammāṭ, who said, 'I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) [and in another version: Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him)]'

'When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of Hell into Hell, then what [happens next]?' So Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) said, 'If Allah wishes to create another creation and make a world for them to return to, He will do so – and I am not saying to you that this is what He will [surely] do.'

key_terms.دُنْيَا: World (in this context, a new worldly realm)

ai.seo_question: What happens after people enter Paradise and Hell permanently?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) addresses the eschatological question of the eternal state of inhabitants in Paradise and Hell, suggesting that Allah may create a new creation and world for them to return to if He wills. This narration highlights the distinction between definitive revelation and plausible theological speculation (ghayb), reflecting the Shia scholarly approach to leaving certain aspects of the unseen to Divine Will rather than asserting them as absolute dogma.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 17.Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Abū Khālid al-Qammāṭ[1] who said, “I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) [and in another version: Abū Jaʿfar (a)],

‘When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise and [throws] the people of Hell into Hell, then what [happens next]?’ So Abū Jaʿfar (a) said, ‘If Allah wishes to create another creation and make a world for them to return to, He will do so – and I am not saying to you that this is what He will [surely] do.’”
